subject: Food Science
title: GMOs: Golden Rice Debate
description: A 60-second lesson on GMOs: Golden Rice Debate.

hook.text: 250,000 children go blind each year from vitamin A deficiency. Golden Rice—engineered to produce beta-carotene.

buildup.text: Ingo Potrykus and Peter Beyer created Golden Rice in 1999—inserting daffodil and bacterial genes into rice to produce.

discovery.text: A single cup of Golden Rice provides 50% of daily vitamin A needs. It's designed for subsistence farmers who can't access.

twist.text: Greenpeace and anti-GMO groups have campaigned against Golden Rice since 2001. Field trials were vandalized.

climax.text: Over 150 Nobel laureates signed a letter in 2016 urging Greenpeace to stop opposing Golden Rice.

punchline.text: A rice that makes vitamins. Free to farmers. Blocked for 25 years by ideology.

quiz.question: How long was Golden Rice delayed after its creation before first approval?
options: 22 years—the Philippines approved it in 2021, created in 1999
